grammarSchedule.why: haben, sein and every modal are A1 words, so war, hatte and wollte are available from the first A2 lesson with no new vocabulary at all
sich erinnern arrives in lesson 2, sich ausruhen in lesson 6 and sich beeilen later; the pronoun paradigm can start on the first of them
kochen, waschen, putzen, bauen and reparieren in lesson 8 are the verbs whose object is worth making the subject: die Küche wird geputzt
traurig, wütend, müde and stolz in lesson 10 are the first A2 adjectives that sit in front of a noun: ein müder Kollege
bestellen, buchen and die Speisekarte in lesson 11 give the situation the polite forms exist for: ich hätte gern, könnten Sie
dass is taught in lesson 12 and weil is already an A1 word, so both connectors are available at the same point
wenn is taught in lesson 12 alongside dass
the prefix only rejoins inside a subordinate clause, so this waits one lesson after weil and dass; A1 supplies anrufen, aufstehen and einkaufen
zwischen, gegen and entlang are taught in lesson 14, and A1 already supplies the rooms and places they govern
niemand is taught in lesson 17; the bank has no separate row for jemand, so the pair is anchored on the negative member
gesund, stark and schwach in lesson 29 and schwer against leicht in lesson 30 are the first A2 adjectives worth putting on a scale
